Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

fastrel 1.0.0

  • Breaking: fastrel_inv() now returns a dgCMatrix, which stores both triangles of the matrix, instead of a dsCMatrix, which stores only one: MCMCglmm::MCMCglmm() (version 2.36) silently gives wrong results with the latter. The new argument matrix_class = "dsCMatrix" still returns the leaner symmetric class, for software that reads it correctly, such as spaMM.
  • fastrel_inv() is tested in animal models fitted with spaMM and MCMCglmm.
  • The documentation calls the additive relationship the genetic covariance (Emik and Terrill 1949), and says between what it is a covariance.
  • New hex logo.

fastrel 0.9.0

  • Breaking: when no column of ped has a recognised name, fastrel_ped() and rel_add() now take the first three columns as the individual, its father and its mother (instead of mother then father). This aligns with the order used by fastrel_vec(), kinship2::kinship() and standard animal breeding pedigrees. sim_ped() and sim_pop() return their columns in the same order (id, dadid, momid).
  • New website, built with pkgdown: https://courtiol.github.io/fastrel/.
  • New rel_copy(), which returns an independent copy of a store (a store is otherwise shared, not copied, when it is assigned).
  • New fastrel_inv(), which returns the inverse of the relatedness matrix (the precision matrix used by animal models) as a sparse matrix, built directly from the pedigree. Matrix is now imported.
  • The results are now also validated in the tests against nadiv::makeA(), and the README compares the speed of fastrel with that of nadiv.
  • Documentation slightly reworked.

fastrel 0.8.0

  • Breaking: rel_new(remember_removed = ) now takes "none" (the default), "fingerprint" (formerly TRUE) or "id", instead of FALSE or TRUE.
  • Breaking: rel_load() only reads stores saved by this version of fastrel.
  • When no column of ped has a recognised name, fastrel_ped() and rel_add() still take the first three columns as the individual, its mother and its father, but now say so in a message, once per R session.
  • New rel_new(remember_removed = "id"), which keeps the identifiers of the individuals removed rather than a fingerprint of each of them. It takes more memory but can never mistake a new identifier for a removed one. rel_save() and rel_load() keep the kind of trace used.
  • Preparation for CRAN: references with DOIs in the description of the package, stricter checks of the arguments of sim_ped() and sim_pop() (single whole numbers or probabilities, no NA), canonical CRAN links in the README, and unused packages removed from Suggests.

fastrel 0.7.0

  • New argument sim_ped(numeric_ids = TRUE) to simulate a pedigree with integer identifiers and 0 for unknown parents, which can be given as it is to fastrel_ped(), rel_add(), kinship2::kinship() or ggroups::buildA().
  • 0 can now be used to define an unknown parent everywhere (synonymous with NA).

fastrel 0.6.2

  • The results are now validated in the tests against kinship2 and ggroups, two independent implementations, for all four measures and on pedigrees of many shapes (inbreeding, selfing, unknown parents, unsorted rows, removals from a store, …).
  • The section “Range of values” moves from the help page of the package to ?relatedness_metrics.

fastrel 0.6.1

  • Documentation only. In ?relatedness_metrics, the table is split in two (it was too wide for the PDF manual) and the link to cov2cor() is fixed. The README is refreshed and explains how to build the manual.

fastrel 0.6.0

  • fastrel_ped(), fastrel_vec() and rel_get() gain an argument metric to return, besides the additive relationship ("additive", the default), the kinship coefficient ("kinship"), Wright’s coefficient of relationship ("wright") or Hamilton’s regression coefficient of relatedness ("hamilton"). The conversion uses no extra memory and adds little time.
  • New help page ?relatedness_metrics defining these measures, with references.
  • Breaking: fastrel_vec() has the arguments sex and chrtype of kinship2::kinship() instead of ...; any other argument is now an error.

fastrel 0.5.1

  • The documentation states the range of relatedness values (0 to 2, above 1 only with inbreeding).

fastrel 0.5.0

  • Tibbles are supported. This fixes fastrel_vec(), which returned a wrong 1 x 1 matrix when each argument was a tibble with one column instead of a vector.
  • Inputs that cannot be a vector of identifiers now raise a clear error.

fastrel 0.4.0

  • Breaking: relatedness_fast() is replaced by fastrel_vec() (same function) and fastrel_ped(), which takes the pedigree as a data frame; the argument carrying of sim_pop() is now K.
  • fastrel_ped() and rel_add() find the columns for the individual, its mother and its father by their names (id, mom, dad, sire, dam, …), whatever their order; the other columns are ignored.
  • New benchmark of memory use, inst/benchmarks/memory_benchmark.R.
  • The documentation defines “store” and “slot”, and its memory figures were corrected after measuring them.

fastrel 0.3.1

  • New argument rel_new(remember_removed = TRUE) to refuse adding again an individual that was removed from a store, which would otherwise come back as unrelated to its relatives. Recommended for metapopulations, whose handling is now documented.

fastrel 0.3.0

  • Breaking: rel_new() no longer has a capacity argument, as the store now sizes itself; sim_ped() and sim_pop() no longer have a seed argument (call set.seed() beforehand).
  • Much faster relatedness_fast(), rel_add(), rel_remove() and sim_pop(), without using more memory.
  • New rel_ids() listing the individuals in a store.
  • Bug fixes: rel_add() leaves the store unchanged when it fails; NA identifiers, invalid arguments of the simulators and stores read back with readRDS() now raise clear errors instead of giving wrong results.
  • The package is checked on GitHub Actions.

fastrel 0.2.1

  • Revised README.

fastrel 0.2.0

  • New rel_save() and rel_load() to save and restore a store.
  • New sim_pop() simulating a population with births, deaths, emigration and immigration.

fastrel 0.1.0

  • First version: relatedness_fast(), the incremental store (rel_new(), rel_add(), rel_remove(), rel_get()) and sim_ped().
